doc.title: Bob Havens interviewed by Monk Rowe, Chautauqua, New York, September 12, 1997

title: Improvisation coming naturally
summary: Havens says improvising and playing by ear came easily to him, and he stays within what he can hear.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: Well improvisation was something that came to me easy. I didn’t ever really have to practice on that. It just was a natural thing that came to me. And I feel really fortunate that I grew to like jazz music and I fortunately have no problem in learning it, you know, picking it up. I can hear something and I can play it on my horn right away. Just anything that I can hear I can play it on the horn. And of course you sort of automatically create a
situation in your mind where you usually hear things that you know you can play on the horn.
If you can’t play it you can’t hear it.
You usually automatically kind of keep within your boundaries on the things that you sort of cook up in your mind.
